..FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...

...UPDATED AVIATION DISCUSSION...

Additional cooling is expected for Friday, which will bring 
temperatures in most places to below average. Below average 
temperatures are expected to continue through next Thursday. The 
pressure gradient has begun to trend onshore ahead of an approaching 
upper level low. This will lead to increased cloud coverage across 
much of the coastal basin for Friday. Periods of clouds can be 
expected through the weekend into early next week. 

The aforementioned upper level low will dig south and move east into 
Northern Baja on Friday. This will bring periods of rain to the area 
by early Friday morning. The highest chances of rain for this first 
period of rain are along the coast. Additionally, there is potential 
for isolated thunderstorms to develop over the waters, locally into 
some coastal communities. The thunderstorm chances are largely 
focused to coastal waters and the coast due to the temperature 
difference between sea surface temperatures (running well above 
average for this time of year) and the cold temperatures associated 
with the passing low pressure system. High resolution guidance is 
picking up on an increase in instability with CAPE values increasing 
to 500-1000 J/kg early Friday morning. There is some potential for 
thunderstorms to locally reach coastal communities but atmospheric 
instability drops drastically the further inland you go, which will 
limit thunderstorm potential. Where thunderstorms develop, expect 
erratic winds and locally heavy rain that may lead to localized 
flooding. Rainfall Friday morning is generally expected to be on the 
lighter side for inland areas. Isolated rainfall rates of 0.40-0.60 
inches per hour are most likely to develop along the coast where 
thunderstorms or heavier rain develops. Chances of rain decrease 
during the day Friday, but isolated light showers at times cannot be 
ruled out. Through Friday afternoon, rainfall totals will largely be 
0.20 inches or less, but some isolated totals over 0.50 inch are 
possible along the coast. 

Rainfall chances increase again Friday evening as another upper 
level low moves east through Central California. This will bring 
another round of rain Friday evening into Saturday, which is 
expected to be more widespread across the coast, valleys, and 
mountains. Peak rainfall rates of 0.20-0.30 inches per hour are 
expected during this time. Rainfall totals for the coast and 
valleys will be largely 0.20-0.50 inches, with totals in the 
mountains closer to 0.50-1 inch. Less than 0.10 inch is expected 
in the deserts. Rainfall is expected to taper off from north to 
south late Saturday morning through the early afternoon. Dry 
conditions look likely for Saturday evening into Sunday. Snow 
levels Friday into Saturday are expected to stay above 8000 ft, 
with up to 2 inches of snow above 8500 ft. 

Another low pressure system is expected to dig south along the West 
Coast Monday and east late Monday into Tuesday. Ensemble guidance is 
in good agreement in the timing of this trough, with lower 
confidence in how far south the low will dig. The ultimate depth of 
the trough will be a big influence on rainfall totals and snow 
levels. NBM chances of rainfall totals exceeding 0.50 inch from 
Monday morning through Wednesday morning are 30 to 45 percent for 
the coast and valleys and 60-70 percent for the mountains. By 
Tuesday morning, spread in NBM snow levels ranges from 5200 ft to 
8300 ft. 

Winds are expected to increase over the mountains and deserts with 
each passing system. Expect a slight increase in winds this
evening, with a more noticeable increases Friday evening into 
Saturday. Peak gusts Friday evening into Saturday will be mainly 
35 to 45 mph, with gusts up to 55 mph through wind prone passes. 
Winds are expected to increase again early next week with the next
trough passage, with the track of the low the main determining 
factor in expected wind speeds. A more southerly track would bring
us stronger winds compared to a more northerly track. 

Additional precipitation and winds are possible for the latter half 
of next week, but there is low confidence in details. Continue to 
monitor the forecast for more information.
